def: The act or ceremony of consecrating; the state of beingconsecrated; dedication.Until the days of your consecration be at an end. Lev. viii. 33.Consecration makes not a place sacred, but only solemny declares itso. South.
The state or quality of being literal. Sir T. Browne.
The capability of being placed or located. [Obs.] Barrow.
The chief harpooner, who also directs in cutting up the speck,or blubber; -- so called among whalers.

The root of a plant (Jateorrhiza Calumba, and probably Cocculuspalmatus), indigenous in Mozambique. It has an unpleasantly bittertaste, and is used as a tonic and antiseptic. [Written also colombo,columbo, and calombo.] American calumba, the Frasera Carolinensis,also called American gentian. Its root has been used in medicine asbitter tonic in place of calumba.
Any one of several species of sea birds of the genus Uria, orCatarractes; a guillemot.
One who receives, or its entitled to receive, an annuity. Lamb.
Excess in eating; extravagant indulgence of the appetite forfood; voracity.Their sumptuous gluttonies, and gorgeous feasts. Milton.
Divination by means of a child's navel, to learn how manychildren the mother may have. Crabb.
